speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you describe exactly where in your neck and arms you are feeling pain, tingling, or weakness? Also, did any specific injury or activity trigger the start of these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain radiate down a specific arm, and do you have difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning your shirt? I need to know if the weakness is symmetric or if it affects one hand more than the other to distinguish between cervical radiculopathy and diabetic neuropathy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and bilateral hand weakness strongly suggests a lower motor neuron process rather than a simple radiculopathy. I need to rule out cervical spondylotic myelopathy or ALS, so I will request imaging and electrophysiological studies. REQUEST TEST: Cervical MRI, EMG_NCS
